newsitem.title: USA: Service Corp launches offer for Loewen.
newsitem.headline: Service Corp launches offer for Loewen.

text.p: Service Corp International said it has taken its proposal to buy Loewen Group Inc directly to the company's shareholders in an exchange offer valued at $45 per share.
The action comes after Loewen's board of directors last week rejected Service Corp's unsolicited offer to buy the company in a transaction valued at $43 per share, or $2.8 billion.
Based on approximately 65 million outstanding shares of Loewen, the offer is valued at about $2.9 billion.

Prior to the exchange of Loewen stock, Service Corp said it plans to reorganize to form New Service Corp International, making Service Corp a subsidiary of the new company. Stockholders of Service Corp would become stockholders of New Service Corp on a one-for-one share basis.

Holders of Loewen common stock will be offered $45 worth of common stock of the new company. Holders of Loewen Series C preferred stock will receive an offer to exchange their shares for $29.51 worth of New Service Corp stock.
Service Corp said the offer is not conditioned on pooling-of-interest accounting.

It also said that it would be willing to raise its bid if the two companies entered a negotiated agreement that was based on a pooling. It said the amount of any increase would depend upon discussions between the two companies.
Service Corp also said it filed suit against Loewen in U.S. District Court in Houston, contending Loewen does not have the standing to seek to block the exchange offer under antitrust laws.

Service Corp said the complaint also contends that Loewen has intefered with its relationship with Loewen shareholders by making misleading statements about Service Corp's business and failing to fully disclose terms of its recent acquisitions of Rose Hills Memorial Park and Mortuary and Prime Succession Inc.

The exchange offer is conditioned on the tendering of at least 75 percent of outstanding common shares of Loewen and 75 percent of Loewen preferred stock. It also calls for the redemption of Loewen's poison pill, the resignation of at least a majority of Loewen's board of directors, government and regulatory approvals and apprroval by Service Corp stockholders.

The exact number of new Service Corp shares and exchangeable shares will be determined based on the trading price of Service Corp's stock on the 20 consecutive trading days ending three days prior to the expiration of the offer, provided that not more than 1.76471 shares would be exchanged for Loewen common stock and not more than 1.15719 shares will be exchanged for the preferred stock.
